accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes WLAN/Wi-Fi communication?
o: It operates exclusively through geostationary satellites
It uses radio waves over a short range
It requires a wired backbone between every pair of devices
It uses only infrared waves over a long range
accepted.x: WLAN or Wi-Fi uses radio waves for short-range wireless communication. It does not require every communicating device to have a separate wired connection.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining medium and range of the technology.
accepted.sec: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Wi-Fi Direct is primarily used to:
o: Connect only satellites to ground stations
Link devices directly without a conventional LAN
Replace radio waves with optical fibre
accepted.x: Wi-Fi Direct enables compatible devices to communicate directly without being connected through a conventional local area network.
accepted.tq: Apply the core function of a named communication standard.
accepted.sec: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Wi-Fi 6 — IEEE 802.11ax
2. Wi-Fi 7 — IEEE 802.11be
3. Wi-Fi Direct — IEEE 802.11be
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to IEEE 802.11ax and Wi-Fi 7 to IEEE 802.11be. Wi-Fi Direct is a device-to-device connectivity feature, not the designation of IEEE 802.11be.
accepted.tq: Use precise standard-number matching and eliminate the swapped technology.
accepted.sec: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology is based on:
o: Reading tags only through optical fibre
Using high-altitude balloons as signal repeaters
Transmitting data exclusively through visible light
accepted.x: RFID identifies objects by wirelessly reading radio-frequency tags. It does not require direct optical-fibre transmission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operating principle of a named access technology.
accepted.sec: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Kavach track tags, as an example of RFID application, are used in a system involving:
accepted.x: Kavach track tags are cited as an example of RFID, in which radio tags are read wirelessly for identification or tracking.
accepted.tq: Connect a real-world example with its underlying technology.
accepted.sec: Wireless and alternative access - WLAN, RFID, CCTV, Project Loon, PM-WANI, Wi-Fi 6/7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Near Field Communication (NFC) generally operates over a range of:
accepted.x: NFC is a very short-range wireless communication technology, generally operating over a distance of a few centimetres.
accepted.tq: Recall the characteristic range rather than confusing it with satellite distances.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bharat 6G Vision document:
1. It seeks to enable India to lead the design, development and deployment of 6G.
2. The target year for this objective is 2030.
3. The document was released in March 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bharat 6G Vision document was released in March 2023 and aims for India to lead the design, development and deployment of 6G by 2030.
accepted.tq: Combine objective, target year and release date in a coded statement question.

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations is correct regarding the TRAI recommendations of February 2026?
o: Auction of all available spectrum across nine bands; uniform 35% spectrum cap; new-entrant net worth reduced from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore per service area
Auction across nine bands; no spectrum cap; net worth reduced to Rs 25 crore
Auction across five bands; uniform 50% cap; net worth increased to Rs 200 crore
Administrative assignment across nine bands; uniform 35% cap; net worth retained at Rs 100 crore
accepted.x: TRAI recommended auctioning all available spectrum across nine bands, a uniform 35% spectrum cap, and reducing the new-entrant net-worth requirement from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore per service area.
accepted.tq: Check all components of a multi-part policy recommendation together.
accepted.sec: Spectrum - auctions, Telecommunications Act 2023, satellite spectrum

accepted.s: At the reserve price, the spectrum proposed for auction under the February 2026 recommendations was valued at approximately:
accepted.x: At the reserve price, the value of the spectrum was approximately Rs 81,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Recall the reported reserve-price estimate rather than the policy percentages.
accepted.sec: Spectrum - auctions, Telecommunications Act 2023, satellite spectrum

accepted.s:
With reference to the Supreme Court decision of February 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Telecom companies do not own spectrum.
2. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code can restructure spectrum rights in the Aircel case.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held that telecom companies do not own spectrum. It also held that the IBC cannot restructure spectrum rights in the Aircel case, making statement 2 false.
accepted.tq: Use the negative legal conclusion to identify the reversed statement.
accepted.sec: Spectrum - auctions, Telecommunications Act 2023, satellite spectrum

accepted.s: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 represents a shift from:
accepted.x: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 moves from a licensing framework to a light-touch authorisation framework.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related regulatory terms.

accepted.s: Under the July 2026 rule of the Department of Telecommunications for infrastructure providers, telecom data and logs must be stored:
o: Only in the country of the equipment manufacturer
accepted.x: The Department of Telecommunications rule requires all telecom data and logs of infrastructure providers to be stored in India.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority and location attached to a data-localisation requirement.

accepted.s: How is satellite spectrum assigned under the First Schedule of the Telecommunications Act, 2023?
o: Through allocation by private satellite companies
Through first-come, first-served auctions conducted by the ITU
accepted.x: Satellite spectrum is assigned administratively under the First Schedule of the Telecommunications Act, 2023, rather than being auctioned.
accepted.tq: Distinguish administrative assignment from auction-based allocation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes GEO satellites from LEO satellites?
o: GEO satellites are about 35,786 km above Earth and have higher latency, whereas LEO satellites are below about 2,000 km and have lower latency
GEO satellites always have lower latency than LEO satellites because they remain fixed over one spot
GEO satellites orbit below 2,000 km, whereas LEO satellites orbit at about 35,786 km
Both GEO and LEO satellites operate at the same altitude and have identical latency
accepted.x: GEO satellites are approximately 35,786 km above Earth, remain fixed over one spot and have higher latency. LEO satellites are below about 2,000 km and generally provide lower latency.
accepted.tq: Compare altitude, apparent position and latency in a single table-based question.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about geostationary communication satellites is correct?
o: They remain fixed over one spot and are located about 35,786 km above Earth
They are used only for personal mobile communication
They necessarily provide lower latency than LEO satellites
They form large constellations below 2,000 km
accepted.x: GEO satellites are positioned at about 35,786 km and appear fixed over one spot on Earth. Their greater distance generally results in higher latency than that of LEO satellites.
accepted.tq: Use the altitude-and-orbital-behaviour pair as the identifying feature.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of a GEO satellite series, with GSAT-7 and GSAT-7A being associated with defence?
accepted.x: The GSAT series is cited as an example of GEO satellites, and GSAT-7 and GSAT-7A are associated with defence applications.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite series with its orbital category and use.

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of LEO satellite constellations?
o: Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper
accepted.x: Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper are identified as LEO constellations. The GSAT examples listed are GEO satellites.
accepted.tq: Separate the LEO group from the nearby GEO examples.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Starlink and OneWeb in India?
o: Starlink has more than 8,000 LEO satellites and obtained its GMPCS licence in India in 2025, while OneWeb earlier received an LoI
Starlink operates only GEO satellites and OneWeb obtained its licence after 2025
OneWeb has more than 8,000 GEO satellites and Starlink received only an LoI
Both companies received their Indian GMPCS licences in 2023
accepted.x: Starlink has more than 8,000 LEO satellites and received its GMPCS licence in India in 2025. Eutelsat OneWeb, associated with Bharti, had earlier received a letter of intent.
accepted.tq: Track company, constellation type, licence status and sequence of regulatory approval.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: GMPCS stands for:
o: Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite
Global Microwave and Private Communication System
accepted.x: GMPCS means Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite. It is the Department of Telecommunications licence required for satellite communication operators.
accepted.tq: Expand the exact acronym without substituting a similar satellite term.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a condition associated with the GMPCS licence for satellite communication operators?
o: Mandatory manufacture of all satellites in India within five years
accepted.x: The conditions include geofencing, no cross-border spillover, lawful surveillance and terminals made in India within five years. The requirement concerns terminals, not mandatory manufacture of all satellites in India.
accepted.tq: Find the option that changes the exact object of a regulatory condition.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Under the stated GMPCS conditions, terminals are required to be made in India within:
accepted.x: One of the GMPCS conditions is that terminals must be made in India within five years.
accepted.tq: Recall the compliance period attached to the licence condition.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the allocation of orbital slots by the International Telecommunication Union?
o: They are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis
They are assigned exclusively to LEO operators
They are allocated after satellites complete their missions
They are allocated only through national auctions
accepted.x: The ITU gives orbital slots on a first-come, first-served basis.
accepted.tq: Identify the allocation principle of the international body.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS

accepted.s: Satellites are required to be de-orbited within what period after the end of their mission?
accepted.x: The stated rule requires satellites to be de-orbited within 25 years of the end of their mission.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact post-mission orbital-disposal period.
accepted.sec: Satellite communication - GEO vs LEO (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), GMPCS
